title.narrative: Integrated Health, Nutrition, WASH and MPCA support to IDPs in Mekelle City IDPs, Abiy Adi town IDPs, and Northwest Zone, Asgede woreda IDPs, Tigray Region, Ethiopia.

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project is a contingency plan aimed at enhancing preparedness and delivering an integrated multisectoral response during emergencies. The IRC will provide critical support in ES/NFI, Health, Nutrition, WASH, and Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) to reduce morbidity and mortality among IDPs in Tselemti woredas (Tahitay Tselemti, Lalay Tselemti, and Mai-Tsebri Town) in the Northwest Tigray zone. Targeting ltbrgt21,537 vulnerable individuals, the project will deliver comprehensive lifesaving services, with robust protection measures mainstreamed across all sectors. Recognizing the fluid nature of crises, the plan is adaptive, with target locations and beneficiaries adjustable based on real-time population movements and informed by needs assessments. ltbrgtThe May 2023 HeRAMS baseline assessment revealed that 79% of the population lacks access to essential primary healthcare services. To address this, the project will enhance preparedness by empowering communities in epidemic readiness, strengthening primary healthcare through personnel deployment, supporting medical consultations, providing logistical support, and delivering essential drugs and medical supplies from the core pipeline (WHO, EPSS) in consultations with relevant authorities.ltbrgt ltbrgtltbrgtTo maintain the health, security, and dignity of displacement-affected communities in the targeted woredas, the project will preposition essential household items (ES/NFI kits) and WASH-NFI standard kits for 658 households, including 100 kits specifically for persons with disabilities (PWD). The dignity kits will contain sanitary pads, underwear, laundry and bathing soaps, washing basins, jerry cans, toothbrushes, and toothpaste to ensure readiness for immediate distribution. All prepositioned items will be stored at IRC's centrally located Mekele warehouse, ensuring a swift and efficient response to emerging needs, strengthening the resilience and well-being of vulnerable populations during crises.ltbrgtFor immediate WASH needs, emergency assessments will identify and rehabilitate safe water sources. Prepositioned water treatment chemicals, including 70% HTH chlorine, aluminum sulfate, and household water treatment chemicals, will ensure safe drinking water. Emergency water distribution points with temporary storage tanks will be established, and trench latrines will be constructed with sex-segregated areas using eucalyptus poles and plastic sheeting. Hygiene awareness campaigns will focus on preventing cholera and COVID-19 outbreaks through safe hygiene practices. ltbrgtBased on IRC’s experience, the MPCA intervention provides dignity and choice to crisis-affected communities by allowing them to address their priority needs. The Cash Toolkit, integrated with the CommCare application and vulnerability indicators, will identify and select 1073 of the most vulnerable households for MPC assistance. The project will prioritize households with the highest vulnerability scores and those facing protection, health, and nutrition challenges. The MPC will be transferred through a financial service provider by cash on hand/envelope cash transfers. IRC uses CommCare software for client registration and verification with vulnerability scoring. To monitor the effectiveness of the cash-transferring activity, IRC will carry out a Post-Distribution Monitoring (PDM) survey. Protection mainstreaming will also be integrated to prevent affected populations from sexual exploitation and abuse, ensuring it is embedded in multisectoral needs assessments, targeting and verification, delivery, and monitoring of responses consistent with protection principles. ltbrgtThis proposed project aligns with the strategic response objectives of the ES/NFI, Health, Nutrition, and WASH clusters, emphasizing preparedness to effectively address emergencies and ensure rapid, comprehensive support for affected populations.ltbrgt ltbrgtlt/pgt
